newsitem.title: UK: Condom maker LIG profit surge crowns recovery.
newsitem.headline: Condom maker LIG profit surge crowns recovery.

text.p: London International Group Plc, one of the world's biggest makers of condoms, reported a sharp rise in full-year profits Thursday and told shareholders its three-year recovery programme was now complete.

LIG, which also makes rubber gloves for medical and household uses, said pre-tax profits rose 12.6 percent to 29.5 million pounds ($48.3 million) after net restructuring charges of 6.1 million pounds ($10 million) and despite sterling's strength.
Sales climbed to 339 million pounds ($555 million) from 310 million ($507 million).
"This is the end of the recovery. We are back to where we should have been," ebullient Chief Executive Nick Hodges said. "London International is now entering a new phase of its development."
The company has climbed back from disaster in 1994, when it announced losses of 175 million pounds ($286 million).

A series of bad diversifications in the 1980s -- as management panicked that its core businesses faced long-term decline -- led to ill-judged moves into businesses, saddling LIG with hefty restructuring charges and trading losses.

Renewed interest in condoms and rubber gloves in the face of the AIDS threat and a strategy of selling-off non-core businesses helped LIG achieve its target of returning to pre-crash levels of profitability by the middle of 1997.
Profit margins also continued to progress towards the group's 15 percent target, improving to 12.3 percent from 10.1 percent a year earlier, the company said.
